### Session timing {#sec-m2-instructor-timing}

Three hours, for a pair of students who have already completed S1 (and
ideally M1, for the stiffness cross-check to mean anything):

| Time | Activity | Watch for |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:15 | Slides, and the ratiometric idea worked through once on paper | Treating "ratiometric" as a marketing word rather than @eq-m2-ratiometric |
| 0:15–0:45 | The calibration sweep, 12 distances | Backlash: not re-zeroing the micrometer's direction between points |
| 0:45–1:15 | Fitting @eq-m2-decay and choosing the working window | Picking a working point without looking at both curves of @sec-m2-window |
| 1:15–1:35 | The supply-drift run | A supply that will not actually hold a controlled drift — see the extension note below |
| 1:35–2:00 | On the beam: the cross-check masses | Using different masses from M1's own sweep |
| 2:00–2:50 | Analysis template | See below |
| 2:50–3:00 | Budget discussion, and the stiffness cross-check if M1 has also been run | — |

If time is short, drop the supply-drift run (@sec-m2-step-drift) and hand
out the shipped `supply-drift` reference run instead: the ratiometric-vs-
absolute comparison is the lesson, and the shipped data makes it just as
well as a bench run would.

### Expected results {#sec-m2-instructor-expected}

On the shipped synthetic data. [TODO (Paolo)]{.todo}: replace with values
from the reference bench once the Hall sensor, the magnet and the
micrometer stage exist and have been characterized; until then these
describe the generator's design parameters (`tools/synth/params/m2.yaml`),
not measurements.

- Calibration curve: a clearly nonlinear $V(d)$, falling steeply below
  about 5 mm and nearly flat above 15 mm, with the two-parameter fit's
  residuals small and unstructured across the sweep.
- Working window: a region in the middle of the sweep where the resolution
  curve of @eq-m2-resolution and the curvature curve of @eq-m2-curvature
  both sit at acceptable levels — narrower than the full sweep range, and
  worth having students defend their chosen threshold, not just read off a
  crossing point.
- Supply drift: the raw Hall-output channel drifts by roughly the same
  fractional amount as the supply; the ratiometric reading (output divided
  by the measured supply) stays essentially flat over the same run.
- Stiffness cross-check: $E_\mathrm{M1}/E_\mathrm{M2}$ close to 1 — the two
  independent routes to Young's modulus should agree to within their
  combined uncertainty, given both experiments' data come from the same
  placeholder beam.

### Common failures, in the order they happen {#sec-m2-instructor-failures}

1. **The micrometer reading, not the intended step, is not recorded.**
   Backlash means the two differ by a fixed amount depending on direction,
   and a fit against the intended values instead of the actual readings
   picks up a systematic offset that looks like a modelling error.
2. **The working point is chosen by sensitivity alone**, ignoring
   @eq-m2-curvature. A very close working point gives excellent resolution
   and terrible linearity over any real excursion — let a group discover
   this by checking their chosen point's curvature term against the beam's
   actual displacement range.
3. **The supply-drift run's displacement is not actually held fixed** — the
   stage is bumped partway through. Then the "ratiometric correction removes
   the effect" result is confounded with a real displacement change, and the
   comparison proves nothing.
4. **Different masses from M1's sweep.** The cross-check needs the *same*
   forces measured two ways; different masses give two different
   experiments a superficial resemblance to a cross-check.
5. **$n$ is silently changed from 3** without re-deriving anything that
   depended on it (the resolution and curvature formulas both use $n$
   explicitly). If a group wants to let $n$ float, make sure the derived
   quantities are recomputed with the fitted value, not left at the design
   default.

### Discussion questions and where they should land {#sec-m2-instructor-discussion}

**"Why not just work as close to the magnet as possible for the best
resolution?"** Because @eq-m2-curvature grows faster than
@eq-m2-resolution improves, in the near field — send them back to plot both
curves together and find where the trade actually turns over, rather than
assert it.

**"The ratiometric correction made the supply-drift plot flat. Does that
mean supply voltage no longer matters at all?"** No — it matters to first
order only through the *shared* factor $V_\mathrm{cc}$ in
@eq-m2-supply-sens; anything that changes $A$ or $d_0$ (temperature, for
instance) is not corrected by dividing by $V_\mathrm{cc}$, and that is
exactly why the sensor's temperature coefficient stays in the budget as its
own component rather than being assumed away.

**"$E_\mathrm{M1}$ and $E_\mathrm{M2}$ disagree by a few percent. Is the
model wrong?"** Probably not — [the beam rig's clamp
discussion](../../hardware/beam-rig.qmd#sec-beam-clamp) says exactly what to
suspect first: a non-rigid clamp affects strain and deflection differently,
so a real disagreement here is data about the clamp, not a failure of
Euler–Bernoulli theory.

### Assessment rubric {#sec-m2-instructor-rubric}

Out of 100, for the report:

| Criterion | Weight | Full marks means |
|---|:--:|---|
| Sidecar completeness | 10 | Every run reconstructible from its metadata; both channels described |
| Calibration fit | 20 | @eq-m2-decay fitted explicitly (not via a library call), residuals plotted and discussed |
| Working-range choice | 20 | Both @eq-m2-resolution and @eq-m2-curvature shown as curves and the window justified from them, not asserted |
| Ratiometric vs. absolute | 15 | Supply-drift run quantified both ways, with the apparent-displacement figure from @eq-m2-supply-error computed, not just described |
| Stiffness cross-check | 15 | $E_\mathrm{M1}$, $E_\mathrm{M2}$ and their ratio computed and reported with uncertainty, not just "they roughly agree" |
| Uncertainty budget | 20 | Correct sensitivity coefficients; the temperature coefficient correctly treated as an influence quantity, not measured directly |

Deduct across the board for a working range chosen without reference to both
criteria, and for treating "ratiometric" as a feature to mention rather than
an effect to quantify.

### If a group finishes early {#sec-m2-instructor-extension}

- Let $n$ float as a third Gauss–Newton parameter and compare the fitted
  value against the assumed $n = 3$; discuss what a fitted $n$ far from 3
  would mean physically.
- Repeat the supply-drift run with a larger deliberate drift and check that
  the apparent-displacement figure of @eq-m2-supply-error scales linearly
  with the drift, as the formula predicts.
- If [M1](../M1-strain-load/index.qmd) has also been run, propagate the
  full uncertainty of $E_\mathrm{M1}/E_\mathrm{M2}$ including the beam
  geometry's own uncertainty (this handbook's budget does not, by design —
  see @sec-m2-budget) and discuss how much it changes the conclusion.
